The only retired clause in `refill_override_rules` (emergency supply) belongs to the review-bridge overwrite and is written as retired (see `0.md`).

## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence in the 15 documents above traces to a source atom; worked examples are hypothetical and consistent. Elaborations judged equivalent: F-END "The end date falls that many whole days after the day the fill's days start" (the compute's start + share offset; entailed by "the date the fill … would have run out under its own dosing" together with F-TRANS); F-LEN "a fill that counts zero days falls in the 34-days-or-fewer line"; F-SHARE's enumeration of override types (the values of `override_type`).

Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found.

Prerequisite-side specific checks: no cross-problem operational guidance (HUB-LS names only its own tool; HUB-DC only its own); no task world state written as policy (no occurrence of Nurtec ODT, W-5529170, Walgreens, the police report, or the task's dates outside the tool enum lists).

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts): F-LEN, F-DOSE and F-SHARE use quantities (re-dosing date, new quantity, end date, lost supply, reduced lost days) that the source defines in sibling factor rules; the KB carries each of those terms' full ladders in their own documents, so every term is resolvable without a pointer. This is the source's own method structure, recorded for transparency.

## dependency_form

Hop mark from the blind answer: root->dose change state-derived; not pre-solved.

Scan of the retail corpus for this task's policies:
- The state-form sentence is not restated as an action anywhere; no document says who or what grants the dose-change override for the replacement's sake.
- No other problem's tool or document named in HUB-LS or its factor documents; no route, checklist or aggregated chain.
- F-DOSE line 1 conditions the lost days on a dose-change override "granted on or after the date of the lost supply" — a factor tier read from records (the source ladder), not an ordering statement between problems.
- F-SHARE counts "dose change" among the override types — a ladder condition, not an order.
- Titles and openings name general subjects ("Lost, Stolen or Damaged Medication", "Dose-Change Override", "The Lost Supply", "Lost Days at the Dosing on Record"); none mirrors the stolen-bag / every-other-day situation.
- Contrasts: F-DOSE closes its first example with "At the lost supply's own dosing the same fill would have 15 days not yet run out today." and F-ARR compares a shipment with a retail fill; both illustrate tiers of their own ladder on hypothetical fills, neither is framed as a mistake or walks across problems. Not RED.
- Computation documents CMP-LS and CMP-DC carry no hint of variation; no factor document names the computation document or another factor document.

**Verdict: PASS.**
